types.embedding_query_text: VideoGame: An interactive entertainment product designed for play on a video game console or computer. Also called Game, ComputerGame, InteractiveSoftware. Examples: GTA 6, Red Dead Redemption 2, Grand Theft Auto 6, GTA VI.

chosen_type.label: VideoGame
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like 'GTA 6' and 'Red Dead Redemption 2' are specific video games, and schema.org's VideoGame class directly matches the definition and examples provided.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

types.embedding_query_text: GameDeveloper: A company that creates and publishes video games for commercial distribution. Also called GameStudio, SoftwareDeveloper, EntertainmentCompany. Examples: Rockstar Games, Rockstar, Rockstar North.

chosen_type.label: GameDeveloper
chosen_type.definition: A company or organization that develops and publishes video games for commercial distribution.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org lacks a direct class for game developers; 'Rockstar Games' is a company, making 'Organization' the most suitable parent class.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: OnDemandEvent
candidates.comment: An OnDemandEvent, as a PublicationEvent, is a publication event where a program is available on-demand. Also called catch-up TV, podcast release, streaming event. Examples: a TV show episode available for streaming after broadcast, a podcast episode release, a movie available for rent online. Distinct from BroadcastEvent, which is a live or scheduled transmission.

candidates.label: GameServerStatus
candidates.comment: A GameServerStatus is a StatusEnumeration representing the operational status of a game server. Also called server status, game server state. Examples: Online, Offline, Maintenance.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.embedding_query_text: Platform: A hardware or software environment on which a video game is designed to run. Also called Console, System, GamingPlatform. Examples: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X/S.

chosen_type.label: VideoGame
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's VideoGame class aligns with the definition of a platform as a hardware/software environment for games. Mentions like 'PlayStation 5' and 'Xbox Series X' fit as platforms for games.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time expressed in calendar format. Also called CalendarDate, ReleaseDate, LaunchDate. Examples: 2026-11-19, 2025-09-01, 2026-05-01, 2026-06-18.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like '2026-11-19' are calendar dates without time components, matching schema.org's Date datatype exactly.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: MusicReleaseFormatType
candidates.comment: MusicReleaseFormatType is an enumeration describing the format of a music release. Also called release media type, recording format. Examples: CDFormat, DigitalAudioRecording, VinylFormat, CassetteFormat. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the kind of release (e.g., single, EP).

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

types.embedding_query_text: Price: The monetary value assigned to a product for purchase. Also called Cost, RetailPrice, Pricing. Examples: £69.99, $79.99, £89.99, $99.99.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like '£69.99' and '$79.99' are monetary values with currency symbols, aligning with schema.org's MonetaryAmount definition.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification detailing the cost associated with delivering an offer using a particular method. Also called Shipping cost, delivery fee, freight charge, postage cost. Examples: "Standard shipping: $5.99", "Express delivery: $15.00", "Free delivery for orders over $50". Distinct from DeliveryMethod, which describes the method itself, not its cost.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type. Examples: list price, sale price, invoice price, suggested retail price.

candidates.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category. Examples: base price, tax, shipping fee, discount.

types.embedding_query_text: Character: A fictional person or entity within a video game narrative. Also called PlayableCharacter, GameCharacter, FictionalPerson. Examples: Lucia, Jason.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Fictional game characters like 'Lucia' and 'Jason' fit schema.org's Person class, which includes fictional individuals.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role

Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

types.embedding_query_text: FictionalSetting: An imaginary location or environment within a video game's storyline. Also called VirtualLocation, GameSetting, FictionalPlace. Examples: Leonida, Vice City.

chosen_type.label: FictionalSetting
chosen_type.definition: An imaginary location or environment within a video game's narrative or world.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's VirtualLocation describes digital spaces but not specifically fictional game settings. 'Leonida' and 'Vice City' are game-specific locations, making a new type necessary.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A measurable amount of something expressed as a number. Also called NumericValue, Measurement, Count. Examples: 230 million, 447 million.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: Mentions like '230 million' and '447 million' are numeric values, matching schema.org's Quantity datatype.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

chosen_type.label: PhysicalCopy
chosen_type.definition: A physical version of a digital product, such as a video game on disc or cartridge.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org lacks a direct class for physical copies of games. The mention 'PhysicalCopy' describes a tangible product, so 'Product' is the most suitable parent.

candidates.label: PhysicalExam
candidates.comment: A PhysicalExam, as a MedicalEnumeration, is a type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Also called medical check-up, physical assessment, health examination. Examples: general physical, sports physical, pre-employment physical. Distinct from MedicalTest, which is a specific diagnostic procedure.

candidates.label: MedicalImagingTechnique
candidates.comment: An enumeration of medical imaging modalities typically used for diagnostic purposes. Also called imaging method, diagnostic scan type, radiology technique. Examples: "MRI", "CT scan", "X-ray", "Ultrasound", "PET scan".

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: SizeSpecification
candidates.comment: Properties related to a product's size, including a size code, system, group, and measurements. Also called product dimensions, sizing details, garment measurements, fit specifications. Examples: a shirt with size 'M' (Medium) in 'US' size system, a shoe with 'EU 42' size, a dress with 'Petite' size group.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration
candidates.comment: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration is a media enumeration of IPTC 'Digital Source' codes, providing information about the origin of a digital media object. Also called digital media source types, IPTC source codes, content origin categories. Examples: 'Original', 'Scanned Print', 'Digital Capture', 'Composite'.

candidates.label: DataDownload
candidates.comment: A DataDownload is a downloadable file or portion of a Dataset, making the data accessible for retrieval. Also called downloadable data, data file, dataset download. Examples: A CSV file of economic statistics, a ZIP archive of research images, a JSON file containing survey results.

candidates.label: UserDownloads
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of downloading content. Also called user download, content download, file retrieval. Examples: a user downloading a software update, downloading an e-book, saving an image from a website.

candidates.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A PresentationDigitalDocument is a DigitalDocument file containing slides or used for a presentation. Also called slide deck, presentation file, slideshow. Examples: a Microsoft PowerPoint file, a Google Slides presentation, a Keynote document, a PDF of presentation slides.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific type of permission that can be granted for accessing a digital document. Also called Access level, permission role, document access type. Examples: ReadPermission, WritePermission, SharePermission, CommentPermission. Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermission, which is an instance of a permission granted to a specific entity.

candidates.label: GamePlayMode
candidates.comment: A GamePlayMode is an Enumeration indicating whether a game is multi-player, co-op, or single-player. Also called player mode, game type. Examples: SinglePlayer, MultiPlayer, CoOp.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip

Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries

candidates.label: PlayGameAction

Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: SeekToAction
candidates.comment: The action of navigating to a specific timestamp within a video object, typically using a URL parameter. Also called jump to time, fast forward to, skip to, go to timestamp. Examples: clicking a link that starts a YouTube video at 2:30, using a video player's seek bar.
